title: WPMS/519/2016 of Bhupendra Signh Vs Smt. Shushila Sharma AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Writ Petition (M/S) No. 519 Of 2016
Bhupendra Singh .... Petitioner
Versus
Smt. Sushila Sharma & 7 Others Ö Respondents

Heard Mr. Vinod Nautiyal, Advocate for the
petitioner, and Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the
caveators/respondents no. 1 to 4.
It transpires that Smt. Vimla Rani was the
original owner of the property, in question, and she
entered into an agreement to sale with Tribhuwan
Kishore Sharma on 28.11.1980 and it was registered
on 29.6.1981. Since in executing the sale deed,
certain shortcomings regarding the ceiling had to
overcome, hence it was agreed that such deed shall be
executed within twenty days from the date of receiving
the notice, informing the sanction of required
permission regarding the land ceiling. It appears that
subsequently Smt. Vimla Rani changed her mind. So,
Tribubhuwan Kishore Sharma was constrained to
issue a notice on 23.4.1991. Having sensed the
issuance of such notice or on receiving the same, Smt.
Vimla Rani executed the sale deed soon in favour of
the petitioner Bhupendra Singh, instead of Tribhuwan
Kishore Sharma. Bhupendra Singh claimed himself to
be the tenant in the property since decades ago.
In this backdrop, Tribhuwan Kishore
Sharma filed an Original Suit No. 196/1991 seeking
specific performance of such contract wherein written

2
statement was filed by Smt. Vimla Rani as well as by
Bhupendra Singh and his other associates like
defendant no. 2 Nirmal Singh and defendant no. 4
Harpal Singh. After filing the written statement, all of
them disappeared, even then the Court by way of
making the publication in the newspaper tried once
more to ensure their attendance in order to provide
the opportunity to all the defendants to contest the
matter, but all went in vain. So, the Court was
constrained to proceed the matter ex parte and the
judgment could be delivered on 20.10.1999. Soon
there after an application was made under Order 9
Rule 13 CPC by Bhupendra Singh along with the
delay condonation application. Both such applications
were rejected. Simultaneously, an application was
filed by the decree holder under Section 28(3) of
Specific Relief Act for execution of the sale deed, while
an application under Section 28(1) was filed by the
petitioner for recession of the contract. The
application filed by the decree holder was allowed by
the Court, while the application of the petitioner was
dismissed.
In the light of these facts, Bhupendra Singh
filed the Civil Appeal No. 8/2016 against the judgment
passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 90/2013,
Bhupendra Singh v. Smt. Sushila & Others. Civil
Revision No. 5/2016 was filed by the petitioner
against the order allowing the application of decree
holder moved under Section 28(3) of Specific Relief
Act. Civil appeal and civil revision, both were decided
by the Additional District Judge, Dehradun vide
judgment dated 24.2.2016. It is an elaborate
judgment, wherein the learned Additional District

3
Judge, Dehradun has divulged his anguish, in first
paragraph of the decision, that by itself speaks how
this litigation is being dragged deliberately for the last
35 years by Mr. Bhupedra Singh and his associates
for the reasons best known to them.
Now, the decree is being executed by the
Civil Judge (Junior Division) and, Bhupendra Singh,
who purchased the property on 29.4.1991 or
sometime thereafter, as well as rest of the
respondents, who are the legal heirs of Smt. Vimla
Rani, have been directed to execute the sale deed. On
account of default on their part in executing such
deed, the Court below is taking stringent measures to
execute the sale deed itself.
I feel that there is not the least merit in this
petition. It is hereby dismissed with costs all
throughout.
The executing court will immediately
execute the decree and will not make any further
delay for any reason whatsoever, except in case of stay
by the Honíble Supreme Court.
